DEFINITION · qeva:1:prime@3

Prime number

A prime is a natural number greater than one whose only positive divisors are one and itself.

editorialnumber · arithmetic
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

A prime is greater than one and cannot be written as a product except using one or itself.

EXACT

The compact statement

Let 1:=S(0). For p∈N, Prime(p) iff p>1 and for every d∈N, if there exists k∈N with p=d·k, then d=1 or d=p.

Example

7 is prime. 12 is not prime because 12=3·4 and 3 is neither 1 nor 12.

Boundary / caveat

This is the positive-natural-number definition. Prime elements in general rings require units and associates to be specified.

Assumptions

  • The natural-number structure and its ordinary multiplication are fixed. · Natural number @2

Provenance

Corrects the former Z-versus-positive-natural scope mismatch and makes the divisibility predicate explicit. This is an original QEVA formulation and remains subject to independent review.
